title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, a paradigm that localizes anomalous tokens within text rather than only classifying entire documents. It proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings from BERT-base-uncased with max-pooled subword aggregation and scores anomalies via nearest-neighbor distance. Experiments on three datasets (SMS Spam, Restaurant Review, Grammar) show TokenCore achieves the best average AUROC at both token and document levels compared to six baselines.

match_target.why: The user hint targets TokenCore token-level AUROC on the Grammar dataset. The paper contains only Table 1 (no Table 3); the value 0.6371 is the TokenCore token-level AUROC on Grammar. This is the cheapest claim to verify because it requires only the TokenCore pipeline on the smallest dataset (300 documents).

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score in [0,1] and the Grammar test set (165 documents after 50% split) is smaller than 2,000 examples. The paper prints the value as a fraction (0.6371), so the band is 0.02 absolute.

requirements.stmt: Use BERT-base-uncased as the embedding model for all methods.
requirements.quote: All the methods operate on BERT-base-uncased embeddings with max pooling aggregation.

requirements.stmt: Aggregate subword embeddings to word level using element-wise max pooling.
requirements.quote: the token-level embedding is computed as: etoken = max(e1, e2, . . . , en)

requirements.stmt: Construct a memory bank from word-level embeddings of all normal training documents.
requirements.quote: we extract word-level embeddings from all normal samples in the training set and store them in a memory bank

requirements.stmt: Compute token-level anomaly score as the distance to the nearest neighbor in the memory bank.
requirements.quote: we compute its anomaly score as the distance to its nearest neighbor in the memory bank

requirements.stmt: Aggregate token-level scores to document level using mean pooling.
requirements.quote: To obtain document-level anomaly scores, we aggregate token-level scores across all tokens in the document

requirements.stmt: Use 50% of normal documents as training data; the rest (normal + anomalous) as test.
requirements.quote: We use 50% normal documents as training data, the rest of data are set as testing

requirements.stmt: Evaluate using AUROC and AUPRC metrics.
requirements.quote: We compare TokenCore against 6 anomaly detection methods and use AUROC and AUPRC as evaluation metrics

requirements.stmt: Use Euclidean distance (or the distance metric specified) for nearest neighbor search.
requirements.quote: where d(·, ·) denotes the distance metric (e.g., Euclidean distance)
